note: Run each query with and without the skill on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. Pass = all expected_behavior items met.

evals.query: Build a support bot for an online shop on LangGraph; describe all rules in the system prompt so it decides on its own when to escalate.
expected_behavior: Does not start by writing a LangGraph agent or a long prompt
Produces or asks to fill a decision card first
Names rules 4 and 10 (prompt without branching, no framework by default) and offers an own tool loop
Escalation designed with delivery confirmation and human approval, not a prompt rule

evals.query: Add to the agent's prompt: if the customer asks for the price, quote the discounted price and say the promo lasts until Sunday.
expected_behavior: Moves price to a tool result plus a {price:N} slot filled by the renderer
Puts promo end date into data/tool output, not into the prompt
Prompt diff is empty or only mentions the tool

evals.query: Let the agent remember the whole conversation with each customer; just pass the history into the context.
expected_behavior: Rejects raw history in context
Proposes card/DB for exact data, structured state for checkpoints, vectors with tenant filter and rerank for fuzzy history
Tenant id set by code, cross-tenant test mentioned

evals.query: Review the agent in this repo.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/audit_agent.py and reports its numbers
Maps findings to rule numbers and mechanisms M1-M9
Lists the manual checks the script cannot do
Proposes the smallest fix first

evals.query: We need to recognise the product from the customer's photo; let's just send the photo to GPT and let it say which catalogue item it is.
expected_behavior: Proposes a local pipeline (segmentation/detector + embedder fine-tuned on catalogue + calibrated decide() in code)
Treats 'ask again' as a valid output with a calibrated threshold
Asks for a held-out domain test set and flags licences of weights

evals.query: Add a follow-up: if the customer has not paid, the agent reminds her about the payment after a day.
expected_behavior: Implements the reminder in a scheduler in code, not in the prompt
Checks the 24 h messaging window and sends inside it or hands to a manager
Reminder text rendered from order state with slots

evals.query: The customer sent a payment screenshot; let the agent check it and set the status to 'paid'.
expected_behavior: Refuses to confirm payment from a screenshot
Confirms via CRM/payment webhook or status poll; screenshot only triggers 'we will check'
Status change written by the CRM module with idempotency

evals.query: The manager sometimes replies to the customer from her phone in Instagram while the bot also writes. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Uses echo events to detect manager messages and set takeover
Takeover checked before and after the LLM call
Release by manager or TTL, logged

evals.query: The agent named the wrong colour for the customer's photo again. Add a rule to the prompt so it asks about the colour.
expected_behavior: Starts with a regression fixture from the journal, not with a prompt edit
Names the mechanism (M1/M4) and the owner: vision decide()/COLOUR verdict and the reply schema
Fix is at the owner (Lab ΔE colour check, verdict-driven reply.kind), prompt diff empty
Runs full regression before commit, one change per commit

evals.query: Add a post-generation guard: if the text contains the word 'payment' and there is an escalation, remove the text so the bot does not over-promise.
expected_behavior: Refuses a guard that edits or erases text (rule 18) and cites the empty-reply incident
Proposes a structured reply field or tool that owns promises, with reject → retry → fallback + card
Adds a fixture proving no empty reply is sent

evals.query: Take prices from the captions of our Instagram posts and let the agent quote them; they are all up to date.
expected_behavior: States captions are history (rule 20) and prices come only from the shop DB via slots
Uses captions for outfits, tone, FAQ and historic prices instead
Mentions legal access (export / Instagram Login API) and stopping on 429 without bypassing

evals.query: Fine-tune the recognition model on photos from customer feedback and deploy it right away.
expected_behavior: Measures a baseline and uses a held-out, session-split test once
Defines deploy gates before training and recalibrates the threshold after
Records a negative result instead of deploying it; checks weights licence

evals.query: We are building an agent for an electronics shop on Instagram. Let's put the whole product database with prices and stock into a vector DB and let the agent search by similarity.
expected_behavior: Rejects embedding the whole DB with prices and stock, naming why: identifiers blur (128/256 GB, 15/15 Pro), stale numbers, filters are not similarity, no provenance
Defines the sellable unit (model × storage × colour × condition) and typed attributes first
Routes question types: SQL filters for exact/filter, compatibility table, lexical for names/aliases, vectors only for fuzzy text and docs, live lookup for price and stock

evals.query: A customer sent a photo of a phone and asks how much the same one costs. Let the model determine the model and storage from the photo.
expected_behavior: Uses the identification ladder: own media / EAN or OCR of label or settings screenshot before visual similarity
States storage, RAM and condition are invisible on a photo and must be asked or read from identifiers
Verdict FAMILY/UNSURE leads to a targeted question; price only via slot from the shop DB

evals.query: Our agent runs on a 40,000-character prompt and three .md files with delivery, warranty and discount rules. Turn this into a proper architecture.
expected_behavior: Inventories every statement and classifies it (fact, procedure, branch, schedule, format, prohibition, mapping, knowledge, identity)
Moves facts to data + tools + slots, procedures to state, branches to code or enum fields, long knowledge to retrievable docs
Migrates one statement at a time with a fixture and deletes the prose; prompt shrinks toward ≤ 8000 chars

evals.query: Our agent keeps the last 30 messages plus all tool results in context so it does not forget anything. Customers complain it mentions items they already rejected. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that stale tool results and history are read as current (context.md failure modes)
Moves refs, verdicts and cart into state rebuilt by code every turn; keeps only a few recent turns
Adds input tokens per turn (median, p90) to the journal and a fixture for the rejected-item case

evals.query: The LLM should only generate replies; let's parse everything else with regex and if-else so it is deterministic.
expected_behavior: Keeps decisions in code but uses the LLM for interpretation roles: intent, constraint extraction, reference resolution, query rewriting, signal detection
Each LLM role gets a strict schema and code validation against a source
Warns that regex over open language is mechanism M4

evals.query: Let the agent save whatever the customer tells it (size, city, preferences) straight into the CRM and the product notes.
expected_behavior: The LLM proposes values in a schema; code writes them only with the verbatim quote verified
The shop DB is never written by the agent; derived data is marked and never overrides primary data
Defines source precedence and an 'unknown' path instead of guessing

evals.query: Which vector database and embedding model should we use for the agent's FAQ and memory? Just take Pinecone and OpenAI embeddings, everyone uses them.
expected_behavior: Starts from question types and a labelled query set from real chats, not from a vendor
Compares the store already in use + a local multilingual embedder + a local reranker against one hosted option on recall, latency, cost, privacy
Requires hybrid lexical + dense, a reranker, metadata filters with tenant, and model name/version stored for re-indexing
Checks licences (e.g. non-commercial embedder weights)
